source.display_title: 05/26/2026 - Marian G. Samson x Andrew Musial  — Undetermined

setter.evidence: No KFS/KL/DH suffix in the title and no setter named in the recorded portion. An application does exist and the rep had read at least part of it: 'And I saw in the application that you run your own company, correct?' Whether a setter or a self-serve form produced it is not determinable from the recording.

prospect.name: Marian Samson
prospect.aka: Titled 'Marian G. Samson' in the file name
prospect.occupation: Runs his own company. Work is management, driving and site visits with very little physical labour — he estimates roughly 70% of the day seated between the desk and the car. Out of the house from around 6.30-7am until about 6pm. Describes the work as 'pretty stressful sometimes'.
prospect.family_status: Two daughters, one 12 and one almost six. Describes them as quiet children who play with dolls, but says that when they do run around 'I cannot keep, I cannot, I think I'm too fat for that.'
prospect.training_background: Largely untrained. Did heavy gym work last year on a friend's encouragement while using anabolic steroids — 'because of the steroids, you get a lot of power... you're like a monster' — and stopped because 'it was not good for my health'. Otherwise only occasional bodyweight work such as push-ups. Two weeks before the call he bought 10 kg and 16 kg kettlebells and began training at home from Trevor's free online videos, unsupervised. Wants formal instruction: 'that's why I was thinking about maybe to get the proper lesson.'
prospect.medical: Spinal disc compression, diagnosed roughly three years ago, together with a hunched or bent posture — 'I have a back, bent posture' and 'it's called a disc... like when your disc is broken', which the rep reframed as compression and the prospect accepted. New back pain that began within days of the call, which he attributes to his own unsupervised kettlebell training: 'Maybe I do something wrong.' Right knee injured about ten years ago, never rehabilitated, now unstable and subluxing — 'it's a bit loose... not stable enough. If I make the wrong move, it might be hopping out... you need to pull it back.' Severe left-side hip restriction: he can cross his right leg over his left but not the reverse, 'something blocked over there, it sits very tight'. High blood pressure for a couple of years. Prior anabolic steroid use, discontinued. Sleeping roughly six hours a night. Takes magnesium in the evening and shilajit daily. Self-attributes weight gain partly to elevated cortisol from work stress.

signals: Wants a former self back, with a specific number and a specific date: 'where I would like to land, to have like around 90 kilos... I can remember myself when I was having 90 kilos', which he places 14 to 16 years ago.

Lost ground across a long hard season rather than to one event — a sedentary business, chronic stress, stress eating, a disc diagnosis, an unrehabilitated knee and hypertension accumulating over more than a decade.

Visible regret, expressed about his children: 'sometimes they like to run out, but I cannot keep, I cannot, I think I'm too fat for that', and 'I don't want to be like that daddy, typical daddy look.'

Decision language typical of the avatar — a line already drawn before the call: 'I want to just start with a new lifestyle, new mode. Maybe it has to change. So it's like I decided so it needs to be changed.' He had already bought kettlebells and cut bread, sugar, sodas and fast food two weeks earlier.

COUNTER-SIGNAL: he owns his own company, which is the_optimizer's occupation profile, but nothing else about the presentation is optimisation — at 105 kg with a compressed disc, an unstable knee and high blood pressure he is seeking rescue, not good-to-great.

goals.text: Health above everything else — 'The focus, of course, is my health. I will put this one in the first position'
Get down to around 90 kg from about 105 kg — the weight he was 14 to 16 years ago
Fix his bent posture and the compressed disc in his back
Stop looking like 'that daddy, typical daddy look'
Be able to keep up when his daughters run around, which he currently cannot

Resolve his high blood pressure through training and diet rather than medication — 'if I start to improve my health, and my body health, and how I eat, and what I eat, and when I eat, I think all this, it will go away by himself'
Start a genuinely new lifestyle rather than another short attempt — 'I want to just start with a new lifestyle, new mode'
Learn to perform the kettlebell movements correctly, having likely hurt his back doing them unsupervised — 'that's why I was thinking about maybe to get the proper lesson'

pains.text: Compressed spinal disc diagnosed about three years ago, plus a bent, hunched posture
New back pain that started days before the call, which he links to his own unsupervised kettlebell training — 'For a couple of days ago, yeah, started... Maybe I do something wrong'
Right knee unstable and subluxing since an injury ten years ago that he never addressed — 'if I make the wrong move, it might be hopping out'
Severe one-sided hip restriction — cannot cross his left leg over his right at all
High blood pressure for a couple of years
105 kg at 186 cm, roughly 15 kg above his own target weight
Roughly 70% of the working day spent seated, between a desk and driving, from about 6.30am to 6pm
Sleeping about six hours a night — in bed around 11pm or midnight, up at 6 to 6.30am
Work stress he believes is raising his cortisol and driving fat gain — 'I think it's because of my business. Maybe cortisol level, it's a bit high'
Stress eating he cannot control — 'I'm struggling to not do that... one half of your body says, come, let's eat something more'
Strong sweet tooth against a two-week-old restriction — 'If anything is sweet, it's my favorite food', while having just cut bread, sugar, sodas, fries and burgers
Damage from a year of steroid-assisted heavy training taken on a friend's advice, since stopped — 'it was not good for my health'
Cannot keep up with his own children and names his weight as the reason
No confidence he is performing the movements correctly, having taught himself from videos

objections.raw_quote: But I try my best, you know, it's not like, it's the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me. You can say whatever you want if I don't do it.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the premise rather than fighting it, then converted it into the accountability case: 'Of course, Trevor is the best in this space when it comes to kettlebells, but it's going to be you that's going to be doing the work. He can coach you, he can keep you accountable, but you have to show up every day.' He followed with a motivation argument built on the prospect's children. Well handled, but the prospect did not visibly move on — he changed the subject to his blood pressure.

evidence: The recording is truncated. It ends mid-sentence at 00:18:24, in the middle of the rep's opening line of the consequence frame — 'Look, I'm going to be brutally honest with you. You're 39... We're not getting any younger, you're 105 kilos, the lifestyle that you're living right now, the amount of stress that you have, and the...' — with the prospect's reply 'Very heavy.' and then nothing.

No pillars were presented, no delivery walkthrough, no tiers, no price, no commitment check and no close attempt appear anywhere in the recorded portion. The outcome is not merely unclear, it is absent from the artifact.

Undetermined is used deliberately rather than follow_up: there is no evidence a follow-up was discussed, and equally no evidence the call ended here. The 16 KB file size and the clean mid-sentence cut point to a recording or export failure rather than a short call.

Directional signals up to the cut, for whoever picks this up: intent was high and already acted upon — he had bought two kettlebells, started training, cut bread, sugar, sodas and fast food two weeks earlier, and stated 'I decided so it needs to be changed.' He was also already asking to buy instruction: 'that's why I was thinking about maybe to get the proper lesson, of course. Let's see how we can manage it.'

Counter-evidence: he pre-emptively pushed back on the value of external coaching — 'the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me' — and no money conversation had begun, so affordability is entirely unknown.

notable.note: Two things. First, a data-integrity problem: this transcript is truncated at 00:18:24, mid-sentence, with no ending. The disposition is unrecoverable from this artifact and the file should be re-pulled from Fathom or checked for a second part before this call is counted in any rep or funnel statistic. Second, and the reason this call is worth recovering: it is the clearest clinical-risk case in the batch and simultaneously the strongest sales setup. The prospect is 39, 105 kg, with a spinal disc compression diagnosed three years ago, a right knee that subluxes ('it might be hopping out'), a hip that will not let him cross one leg, and high blood pressure — and he has spent the last two weeks doing unsupervised kettlebell work from Trevor's free videos and has developed new back pain as a result. He half-diagnosed it himself: 'Maybe I do something wrong.' That is the single best argument for paid coaching anywhere in this batch and also the single loudest signal that a clinical screen is needed before selling loaded ballistic training. Nothing in the recorded portion asks whether any clinician has cleared him. On the positive side, this is the only call in the batch where the rep demonstrably used the application ('I saw in the application that you run your own company') and the only one with a genuinely thorough baseline — age, height, weight, occupation, sitting percentage, injuries with duration, diet, energy and working hours were all asked directly. One coaching note visible even in the fragment: the prospect reported sleeping about six hours and the rep replied 'Okay. Not bad.' For a hypertensive 39-year-old with self-identified cortisol-driven fat gain, six hours is a finding, not a pass.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion, plus a truncated recording. Roles read from content throughout. Clear misattributions: at 00:00:55 the frame ('These calls are very simple. I just want to understand...') sits under the prospect's label but is the rep; at 00:09:22-00:10:11 the steroid explanation and the line 'the muscles grow faster than your joints can adapt' are split across labels with the rep's coaching point landing under the prospect; at 00:13:15-00:13:17 the exchange about children is fully inverted, so 'Do you have kids?' appears under the prospect and 'Yeah, I have two daughters' appears under the rep — the daughters are the prospect's, confirmed by his later line 'I cannot keep, I think I'm too fat for that.' Audio quality was poor at the start: the prospect's laptop produced heavy noise and he switched to headphones around 00:01:19, and roughly the first two minutes are consumed by technical issues. The recording then stops mid-sentence at 00:18:24 with no closing. The rep's display label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the title and folder say Andrew Musial; recorded as Andrew Musial, flagged for confirmation.
